violations: CSCF 1.2 [1.2-A1]: VM uses a static SSH key pair (key_name set); privileged access should go through SSM Session Manager, not a persistent shared credential (§ Control Statement). (resource: aws_instance.reporting_host)
CSCF 1.2 [1.2-A2]: VM has no IAM instance profile; SSM-managed, auditable admin access is not available (§ Control Statement). (resource: aws_instance.reporting_host)

CSCF 1.3 [1.3-A1]: VM does not enforce IMDSv2 (token-required metadata). The instance metadata service is a credential-theft / lateral-movement vector (§ guidelines). (resource: aws_instance.reporting_host)
CSCF 1.3 [1.3-A2]: VM allows an IMDS hop limit of 2 (> 1), enabling metadata relay beyond the instance to containers/proxies (§ guidelines). (resource: aws_instance.reporting_host)
CSCF 1.3 [1.3-A3]: VM root volume is not encrypted at rest (§ guidelines). (resource: aws_instance.reporting_host)
CSCF 1.3 [1.3-A5]: VM uses 'default' tenancy; platform-level VM isolation for the Swift secure zone requires dedicated or host tenancy (§ guidelines). (resource: aws_instance.reporting_host)

CSCF 1.4 [1.4-A1]: Secure-zone route sends all IPv4 traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to a NAT gateway. Internet access from the secure zone must be highly restricted or blocked (§ a). (resource: aws_route.pkg_downloads)
CSCF 1.4 [1.4-A4]: No VPC endpoint is configured. AWS-service access from the secure zone should use VPC endpoints rather than egressing to the Internet (§ a, § b).
CSCF 2.3 [2.3-A1]: RDS instance is publicly accessible; attack surface must be minimised (§ adjust vulnerable defaults). (resource: aws_db_instance.reporting_db)
CSCF 2.3 [2.3-A2]: S3 public-access block does not enable all four settings; public exposure is not fully blocked (§ adjust vulnerable defaults). (resource: aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block.exports)

CSCF 4.2 [4.2-A3]: RDS instance does not enable IAM database authentication; database login should not rely solely on a single static password (§ Control Statement). (resource: aws_db_instance.reporting_db)
CSCF 5.4 [5.4-A1]: Secret is not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key; the password repository must use a controlled key (§ logical storage). (resource: aws_secretsmanager_secret.reporting)

CSCF 5.4 [5.4-A4]: RDS master password is hardcoded inline; use Secrets-Manager-managed credentials (manage_master_user_password) instead (§ no hardcoded passwords). (resource: aws_db_instance.reporting_db)

CSCF 5.4 [5.4-A5]: Lambda environment variable 'DB_PASSWORD' hardcodes a password-like value; reference a Secrets Manager ARN instead (§ no hardcoded passwords). (resource: aws_lambda_function.exporter)
